rendered: The authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte. As opposed to using traditional organic carbonate electrolytes, the coin cells used NaPF6 salt dissolved in tetraglyme.[1] The choice built on earlier studies of sodium anode stability in glymes. The electrolyte was chosen to overcome[2] the unstable SEI formation that was observed on Na metal anodes in carbonate-based electrolytes[3]. A stable SEI in the glyme electrolyte is also credited with the high Coulombic efficiency and cycling performance.
